speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing your history. To better understand your current symptoms, can you tell me your age and gender? Also, does the knee pain wake you up at night or occur in the morning?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your age, sexual history, and the pattern of migratory joint pain starting in the ankle and now affecting the knee alongside urinary symptoms, I am concerned about Reactive Arthritis. Did you notice any eye redness or discharge, or any skin rashes on your legs or palms recently?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome)

Please confirm if you have experienced any redness, pain, or blurred vision in either eye recently, and have you noticed any scaly skin rash, particularly on your soles or palms?
